- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops from peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) to dampen volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with cycle phase; shift forecast toward sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days.
